image_description: A close-up view of a grey whale's head and upper torso breaching the water surface. The whale exhibits characteristic mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches, particularly on the rostrum. Water splashes around the lower jaw as it emerges from the blue ocean against a pale sky background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle of the image shows the side profile of the rostrum; the top of the head where blowholes are located is not visible or is obscured by the angle and lighting.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin clearly displays the expected mottled grey coloration with distinct white callosities/barnacle patches on the snout and head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only captures the head and anterior body; the posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be is outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck/shoulder region are visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified from this cropped perspective.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible skin texture matches the description of mottled grey with white barnacle clusters.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or submerged; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located further back on the body and are not visible in this head-focused crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution texture of the skin shows roughness and raised white areas consistent with callosities/barnacles.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The water splash around the jaw lacks individual droplet definition, appearing slightly smudged or painterly rather than physically precise frozen motion. Minor blending between the whale's chin and the water line.
The very tip of the snout appears slightly softened or melted into the background sky, lacking a sharp, crisp edge typical of high-quality photography.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification based on head shape and skin pattern, distinguishing it from other baleen whales like humpbacks or rights.
To assess the overall realism of the water interaction, lighting consistency, and detect subtle generative artifacts in the texture.
To verify the boundary integrity between the whale and the sky/water, checking for edge bleeding or haloing effects common in AI generations.
To ensure the whale is correctly grounded in the water volume and not floating unnaturally or merging with the background depth.

focus_areas: Edge sharpness at the sky-whale boundary
Anatomical correctness of the rostrum arch
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the water splash mechanics; AI often struggles with fluid dynamics, resulting in 'smudged' water. Verify if the barnacle patterns look naturally random or procedurally repetitive. Check the eye region for any structural anomalies or lack of detail.
